conviction_note: A mild long lean: the record-hot Q3 (an industry proxy, partly in a consensus that rose from $1.67 to about $1.72) and a probable outlook roll-forward to 2031, which Entergy also did at Q3 2025 and peer AEP did on 2026-10-28 with a raised range, set against a +9.3% 20-day rebound, modest put skew and a holder base that sold the Q2 print -4.03% on equity dilution. p_up 55 times abs 2.8 gives +0.28. impact_sum is +0.30, so the two measurements agree.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS consensus of about $1.70-1.73. Sources: MarketBeat $1.73 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/entergy-nyseetr-releases-fy-2026-earnings-guidance-2026-07-29/), nextearningsdate $1.70 with revenue $4.15B (https://nextearningsdate.com/entergy.html); AAII had $1.67 in August, so the number has drifted up. Prior-year Q3 2025 was $1.53, which included +$0.06 of weather (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/65984/000006598425000126/earningsrelease3q25_ex991.htm). FY2026 guide is $4.25-4.45 against a $4.40 consensus; YTD adjusted EPS is $1.90, so H2 needs $2.45 for the guide midpoint and about $2.50 for consensus (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000065984/000006598426000279/earningsrelease2q26_ex991.htm). Two estimate sources agree within $0.03, so the bar is treated as sourced.
positioning_check: Short interest was 16.86M shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, about 3.7% of shares outstanding, with 6.11 days to cover. That is down about 1.0M from the prior settlement and down from a peak near 24.9M in mid-June 2026 (https://equibles.com/stocks/etr/shortinterest, read 2026-10-30). This is not a crowded short. The baseline's 25-delta skew is +2.75 vol points (downside paid), which is modest and typical for a utility. Put/call OI ratio is 0.35. ATM IV is 30.6% against 15.7% realised, and the ATM spread is 25.6% of mid, so the 4.37% event-implied move is probably inflated by a wide, illiquid quote. The stock is +9.3% over 20 days and +2.7% over 5 days, rebounding from about $100.91 on 2026-10-02 after XLU's steepest monthly drop in nearly two years with the 10-year above 5.2% (https://247wallst.com/investing/etf/2026/10/02/utility-stocks-are-the-most-oversold-since-2023/). Sell-side targets were trimmed in October: JPM $137 to $130 (OW), Barclays $128 to $115 (OW), MS $98 to $101 (EW); the average is about $120.8 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-entergy-nyse-etr-price-target-raised-to-10100-2026-10-21/).

findings.finding: Q3 2026 was the hottest US summer on record, and every month of the quarter set a national record: July 2026 was the warmest month on record for the contiguous US, August the warmest August, and September the warmest September. Texas had triple-digit record highs on 2026-08-22, and Extreme Heat Warnings covered NW Louisiana, E Texas and S Arkansas. ERCOT set an all-time peak of 91.1 GW and SPP 58.0 GW; MISO reached 121.5 GW, within 4% of its record. Against this, Entergy's Q3 2025 weather contribution was only +$0.06/share. Read across that weather gap, a Q3 EPS print of perhaps $0.05-0.12 above the ~$1.72 bar is plausible, and FY2026 could move toward the top of the $4.25-4.45 guide. YTD weather through H1 2026 was -$0.02.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 printed $1.53 with +$0.06 of weather and a narrowed guide, and the stock moved +0.46%. Q2 2026 beat by $0.02 (weather +$0.01) and the stock fell 4.03% on dilution and YoY decline. Weather-driven beats have not been paid much on this name; the median absolute reaction is 1.76%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus has risen only from $1.67 (AAII, August) to about $1.70-1.73, which is +11-13% YoY. That is consistent with rate actions plus normal weather, not with a record-heat quarter. Had the market fully priced the heat, Q3 estimates would sit well above $1.75 and the FY consensus above $4.40. Still, the weather is public and analysts partly adjust for it, so this is at best partly unpriced.
findings.independence: Peer AEP's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-28) shows vertically integrated retail sales +8.0% and residential +8.9% YoY. AEP beat ($2.23 vs about $2.05) and guided at or above the top of its range (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000004904/000000490426000069/a3q20268kpressreleaseex991.htm). EIA, 2026-10-15, on summer peak records (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=68305). Both are proxies; neither is Entergy's own number. Counter-signal: a LSU climate weekly notes a rare early-August front with below-normal conditions in Louisiana (https://lsu.edu/state-climate-office/losc_reports/weekly_reports/losc-weeklysummary-29jul-04aug2026.pdf).

findings.finding: At Q3 2025 Entergy both narrowed its FY guidance and extended its multi-year outlook. The 2Q26 deck carries a $67B 2026-2030 capital plan and an EPS outlook of >8% CAGR to $7.05-7.35 in 2030. Peer AEP used its 2026-10-28 Q3 print to raise its 2026 range to 'at or above the high end', add 2027/2028 ranges and roll its capex plan to $100B through 2031 with 9-11% EPS growth. A roll-forward to 2031 with a narrowed 2026 range (probably upper half, given the weather) is the likely shape of this print. The guide is what this name trades on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 2025 'narrows guidance range and extends financial outlooks' print moved +0.46% (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/35753953/entergy-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results). Q2 2026 reaffirmed the guide with no extension and moved -4.03%. Feb 2026 (Q4/new year) moved +1.76% and Feb 2025 +5.95%, the largest reaction in the history.
findings.why_not_priced: The pattern of a Q3 roll-forward is known, so part of this is expected. What is not known is the size of the 2031 step and of the capex increase. AEP's raise came after its last outlook, and Entergy's 7-12 GW data-center pipeline (Q4 2025 call) has not been converted into a published 2031 figure. If the market had priced a large step-up, ETR would not trade around $110 against an average target of about $121, after JPM and Barclays cut targets in October.
findings.independence: AEP Q3 2026 8-K, 2026-10-28 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000004904/000000490426000069/a3q20268kpressreleaseex991.htm), a different company and document. The Q3 2025 Entergy precedent comes from Barchart/PRN. The weather finding shares the 'upper half of 2026 range' leg; that leg is sized there, and this finding is sized on the multi-year outlook only.

findings.finding: Entergy's 5-year equity plan is $7B against a $67B capex plan. A May 2026 $2.175B forward (19.25M shares) is still outstanding, and on 2026-09-02 the company settled the 2025 forwards, delivering 11.15M shares for about $913M. A rolled-forward, larger capex plan (see the guidance finding) would most likely come with a larger equity need. This holder base sold the Q2 2026 print -4.03% with dilution cited as a concern.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026, the first print after the $2.175B offering, opened strong and reversed to close -4.03% (high $114.29, close $107.79), with dilution named among the causes (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/filing-royal-bank-of-canada-lowers-stock-holdings-in-entergy-corporation-etr-2026-07-30/).
findings.why_not_priced: The existing equity is priced. A new equity figure tied to a 2031 plan is not yet public. What the money buys was asked and answered: rate base for contracted large-load customers (the Meta Hyperion generation, Google and Avaio in Arkansas), so this is funding visible demand and is sized small. The negative rests only on this name's demonstrated dislike of dilution.
findings.independence: The equity-plan slide in the 2Q26 deck (https://s201.q4cdn.com/714390239/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/2Q26-Presentation.pdf) and the Q2 reaction. This shares the capex roll-forward premise with the guidance finding; it is the cost side of the same event, not a contradiction of it.

findings.finding: ETR enters the print +9.29% over 20 days and +2.74% over 5 days, at $110.28, 6.5% below its 52-week high. The move is a rebound from about $100.91 on 2026-10-02, after XLU's steepest monthly drop in nearly two years with the 10-year Treasury above 5.2%. So the run-up is rates and sector mean-reversion, not company news, and the stock carries less 'cheapness' cushion into a print than it did a month ago. Meanwhile the sell side trimmed targets in October (JPM $137 to $130, Barclays $128 to $115).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 came in after a strong run and reversed intraday from $114.29 to $107.79 (-4.03%). There is no other clean run-up/reaction pair in the 7-print history.
findings.why_not_priced: This is positioning, not information. The +2.75 vol-pt put skew already leans the same way modestly. Short interest is only 3.7% and falling, so there is no squeeze fuel on the upside either.
findings.independence: Analyst PT cuts in October (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-entergy-nyse-etr-price-target-raised-to-10100-2026-10-21/); the baseline skew of +2.75.

findings.finding: Tropical Storm Edouard made landfall near Johnson Bayou, LA on 2026-09-01 and left about 70,000 Entergy Texas customers without power. Tropical Storm Arthur in June caused about 37,000 Entergy outages in Louisiana. Restoration costs are normally deferred to regulatory assets and securitized, so the EPS effect is limited to some Q3 O&M and lost sales.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved print in the baseline turned on a tropical storm of this size.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and small. It is filed so the panel can see it; if the market had treated it as material, Q3 estimates would have come down in September, and they rose.
findings.independence: Separate report of Entergy Texas outages about 70k (https://usahousinginformation.com/tropical-storm-edouard/), low-quality source.

findings.finding: Diluted shares rose to 466M in Q2 2026 from 446M a year earlier, and the 2026-09-02 settlement of 11.15M forward shares adds to the Q3 count. The share-effect drag was -$0.05 in Q2 and will be at least that in Q3. This sits inside the affirmed $4.25-4.45 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Share effect was one of several YoY drags cited in Q2 2026 (-4.03%).
findings.why_not_priced: This is largely priced: the settlements were disclosed and the guide already absorbs them. It is filed near zero for completeness.
findings.independence: The 2026-09-02 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/65984/000006598426000312/etr-20260902.htm) shares the forward-settlement fact with the financing finding. This finding covers only the Q3 per-share mechanics; the financing finding covers the forward equity need.

outside_window.finding: The LPSC final vote on Entergy Louisiana's fast-tracked Meta (Evest) expansion is pending: seven more turbines and about $21B of generation and transmission. Entergy reportedly wants a vote on 2026-11-18; other outlets say December. Commissioner Lewis voted no on both prior Meta items.
The Entergy Arkansas base rate case (docket 26-001-U, filed 2026-02-27, a $44.6M requested deficiency and the first in ten years) has no final order found. A decision is expected around year-end.

baseline_tension: The modest +2.75 put skew and the +9.3% run-up lean against the weather and outlook positives, so p_up was held at 55 rather than higher. The event-implied 4.37% looks inflated by a 25.6%-of-mid ATM spread and IV twice realised, so abs_move was set at 2.8: above the 1.76% median because of the likely outlook roll-forward, below the option number.
lessons_applied: Lessons 1 and 5 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; weather/macro proxy, 'none of what paid was reasoning from weather'): weather finding cut from +0.6 to +0.4, print_vs_bar from +2.0 to +1.5, p_up from 56 to 55.

Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the money funds contracted large-load rate base (Meta, Google/Avaio), so the equity-plan finding was cut from -0.3 to -0.15; it is kept negative only for this holder base's demonstrated reaction to dilution in Q2 2026.
Lesson 6 (resolve inside the window): the LPSC Meta vote (11-18 or December) and the Arkansas rate case were already in outside_window; nothing changed.
Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest of 3.7% with 6.1 days to cover is not crowded, so the positioning negative was left at -0.3.
